content: 1. Eddy K, Vogel J, Comrie-Thomson L, Zahroh R, Bonet M conducted a systematic review protocol that utilized mixed methods to explore the prevention of infections at birth through the use of antibiotics and antiseptics. This protocol is registered under PROSPERO with ID CRD42020191746 and was accessed on March 23, 2021. 2. Weckesser A, Farmer N, Dam R, Wilson A, Morton VH, and Morris RK performed a qualitative pilot study to investigate women’s perspectives on recovery after cesarean section, the risk of infection, and their experiences with the PREPS trial. The findings were published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2019, volume 19, issue 1, article 245. 3. Downe S, Finlayson K, Oladapo OT, Bonet M, and Gulmezoglu AM conducted a systematic qualitative review to identify what aspects of childbirth are most important to women. Their work was published in PLoS One in 2018, volume 13, issue 4, article e0194906. 4. Briscoe KE and Haas DM developed a core outcome set to standardize the reporting of maternal infectious morbidity outcomes related to cesarean delivery. Their research was published in the American Journal of Perinatology in 2020, volume 37, issue 4, pages 436–452. 5. Alekwe LO, Kuti O, Orji EO, and Ogunniyi SO compared the efficacy of ceftriaxone versus a triple-drug regimen in preventing infectious morbidities following cesarean section. Their findings were published in the Journal of Maternal-Fetal & Neonatal Medicine in 2008, volume 21, issue 9, pages 638–642. 6. Deng D, Yuan W, Ding L, and Chen X conducted a clinical study on the coadministration of cefazolin sodium and metronidazole for infection prophylaxis during the perioperative period of cesarean section. This study was published in Pharm Care Res in 2007, volume 7, pages 278–280. 7. Evers S, Goossens M, de Vet H, van Tulder M, and Ament A developed a criteria list for assessing the methodological quality of economic evaluations, known as the Consensus on Health Economic Criteria. This work was published in the International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care in 2005, volume 21, issue 2, pages 240–245. 8. Benigno BB, Ford LC, Lawrence WD, Ledger WJ, Ling FW, and McNeeley SG conducted a double-blind, controlled study comparing piperacillin and cefoxitin for the prevention of postoperative infections in patients undergoing cesarean section. Their findings were published in Surgery, Gynecology & Obstetrics in 1986, volume 162, issue 1, pages 1–7. 9. Purba AKR, Setiawan D, Bathoorn E, Postma MJ, Dik JH, and Friedrich AW performed a systematic review of cost analyses related to the use of prophylactic antibiotics for the prevention of surgical site infections. Their work was published in Frontiers in Pharmacology in 2018, volume 9, article 776. 10. The International Medical Products Price Guide provides information on the pricing of medical products and was accessed on April 20, 2021. 11. The World Health Organization’s Model List of Essential Medicines for Children, 7th edition (2019), outlines essential medicines for pediatric care. This document was accessed on April 23, 2021. 12. Knowles R, Sharland M, Hsia Y, Magrini N, Moja L, Siyam A, et al. measured the availability and use of antibiotics in 20 lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2020, volume 98, issue 3, pages 177–187. 13. Torloni MR, Bonet M, Betran AP, Ribeiro-do-Valle CC, and Widmer M conducted a systematic review to assess the quality of medicines used for life-threatening pregnancy complications in lowand middle-income countries. Their work was published in PLoS One in 2020, volume 15, issue 7, article e0236060.
